stimulus.text: "Let no man of us budge one step, and let slave-holders come to beat us from our country. America is more our country, than it is the whites—we have enriched it with our blood and tears." — David Walker, Appeal to the Coloured Citizens of the World, September 28, 1829
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim public-domain quotation from David Walker, Appeal to the Coloured Citizens of the World (Boston, September 28, 1829). Wording checked against the Documenting the American South electronic edition.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain quotation from David Walker (1829)
stem: Walker’s position differs most directly from the American Colonization Society’s plan in that Walker

options.text: wanted slavery to end only after slave owners were paid
options.misconception: Walker calls for resistance now, not for a paid and gradual end.

options.text: insisted Black Americans should stay and claim rights in the United States
believed Black and white Americans could never live in the same country
options.misconception: That belief belonged to colonization supporters, not to Walker.

options.text: asked white abolitionists to speak for enslaved people
options.misconception: Walker speaks to Black readers himself and calls them to act.

rationales.A: Walker does not ask owners to wait for payment. He calls on Black Americans to resist and to stay.
rationales.B: The Colonization Society wanted free Black Americans sent to Africa. Walker answers: do not budge one step.
rationales.C: Walker argues America is more Black Americans’ country than the whites’. He claims a shared country, not a separate one.
rationales.D: Walker writes to his brethren, not to white abolitionists. He wants Black readers to speak and act for themselves.
rationales.general:
1. Name the Colonization Society’s plan. It sent free Black Americans to Africa.
2. Name Walker’s answer. Do not budge one step; America is more our country than the whites’.
3. Name the split. Both sides opposed slavery, but they differed over staying versus leaving.
Background: The Colonization Society was founded in 1817, and about 12,000 Black Americans went to Liberia by the Civil War.
Remember: two plans can agree that slavery is wrong and still differ over where free people belong.
